# 1 Samuel Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 124v-125r | **Source Image:** 1SA_009_page_001.jpg, 1SA_009_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now there was a man of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a mighty man of valor.

**2** And he had a son, and his name was Saul, a young man and handsome — and there was no man among the sons of Israel more handsome than he; from his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.

**3** And the donkeys of Kish, the father of Saul, were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, "Take now one of the servants with you, and arise, go seek the donkeys."

**4** And he passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and he passed through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. And they passed through the land of Shaalim, but they were not there. And he passed through the land of Benjamin, but they did not find them.

**5** When they came to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, "Come, let us return, lest my father cease being concerned about the donkeys and become anxious about us."

**6** And he said to him, "Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is honored; all that he speaks surely comes to pass. Now let us go there; perhaps he can tell us our way upon which we have gone."

**7** And Saul said to his servant, "But behold, if we go, what shall we bring to the man? For the bread is gone from our vessels, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What do we have?"

**8** And the servant answered Saul again and said, "Behold, there is found in my hand a quarter of a shekel of silver, and I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."

**9** (Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," for he who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer.)

**10** And Saul said to his servant, "Your word is good. Come, let us go." And they went to the city where the man of God was.

**11** As they were going up the ascent to the city, they found young women going out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"

**12** And they answered them and said, "He is; behold, he is before you. Hurry now, for he has come to the city today, because the people have a sacrifice today on the high place.

**13** As soon as you enter the city you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat. For the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice; afterward those who are invited eat. Now go up, for you will find him about this time."

**14** And they went up to the city. As they were coming into the midst of the city, behold, Samuel was coming out toward them, going up to the high place.

**15** Now the LORD had revealed the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came, saying,

**16** "At this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have seen my people, because their cry has come to me."

**17** And when Samuel saw Saul, the LORD answered him, "Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you. This one shall restrain my people."

**18** And Saul approached Samuel in the midst of the gate and said, "Please tell me, where is the house of the seer?"

**19** And Samuel answered Saul and said, "I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, and you shall eat with me today, and in the morning I will send you away, and all that is in your heart I will tell you.

**20** And as for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And for whom is all that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for you and for all the house of your father?"

**21** And Saul answered and said, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And my clan is the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin. Why then do you speak to me in this manner?"

**22** And Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the chamber and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited — and they were about thirty men.

**23** And Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion that I gave to you, of which I said to you, 'Set it aside.'"

**24** And the cook lifted up the thigh and what was upon it, and he set it before Saul. And he said, "Behold, that which has been reserved is set before you. Eat, for it has been kept for you until the appointed time, saying, 'I have invited the people.'" And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.

**25** And they came down from the high place into the city, and he spoke with Saul on the roof.

**26** And they rose early, and it came to pass at the ascending of the dawn that Samuel called to Saul on the roof, saying, "Arise, and I will send you on your way." And Saul arose, and the two of them — he and Samuel — went out into the street.

**27** As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to pass on before us" — and he passed on — "but you, stand here now, and I will make you hear the word of God."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1** — Heb. gibbor chayil: "a mighty man of valor." This designation establishes Kish's social standing as a man of wealth and military distinction among the Benjaminites.

**Verse 2** — The description of Saul's physical stature — "from his shoulders and upward" taller than the people — foreshadows the people's desire for a king of imposing appearance, contrasting with the LORD's later rebuke in 16:7.

**Verse 9** — The parenthetical editorial gloss explains the shift in prophetic terminology: ro'eh ("seer," one who sees visions) was the older term, replaced by navi' ("prophet," one who speaks forth). This note reflects the hand of a later redactor preserving the text for a new generation.

**Verse 15** — Heb. gala 'et-'ozen Shemu'el: Lit. "uncovered the ear of Samuel," an idiom meaning to reveal secretly or disclose privately. The LORD had given Samuel advance notice of Saul's arrival.

**Verse 16** — Heb. nagid: "ruler" or "designated leader," distinct from melekh ("king"). The term nagid implies one appointed by God, whereas melekh carries connotations of sovereign autonomy. The LORD appoints a nagid; the people demanded a melekh.

**Verse 17** — Heb. ya'atsor: "shall restrain" or "shall govern." The root 'atsar means to hold back, contain, or rule. The ambiguity is telling — Saul is appointed both to lead and to restrain the people within bounds.

**Verse 24** — The reserved thigh portion (hashoq) was the priestly portion (cf. Lev 7:32-34), here given to Saul as a sign of his divinely appointed status. The text signals Saul's elevation before the public anointing.

-- LOGOS
